data.hypothesis: The prior correct 128-target/128-source-tile candidate showed that CTA-level source reuse is promising. A 256-target CTA with a 256-source tile should reduce the number of shared-memory staging and synchronization rounds while retaining one thread per target. Its four static shared arrays use 4,096 bytes, within the 49,152-byte limit; the larger CTA may trade some occupancy for fewer tile rounds, so the official per-size geometric-mean comparison is needed.
data.notes: This is the next bounded tile-size point: block/items_per_block 256 and source tile 256, following the previously measured correct 128/128 candidate. No new correctness or timing measurement is claimed here. The prior candidate outcome was valid and correct (mean 0.00105827803570993 s; score 0.6364454057083914), versus the supplied baseline (mean 0.0018526411283622502 s; score 0.5); per-size timings were not provided. The controller should assess this candidate with full correctness and the official per-size geometric-mean protocol. Shared storage is static (4 x 256 x sizeof(float) = 4,096 bytes), so no dynamic shared-memory launch allocation is requested. Inactive target-tail threads still participate in both barriers, and incomplete source tiles are bounds-checked.
transformations: Cooperatively stage each source tile's x, y, z, and mass into four static shared arrays, with bounds-safe filling for partial tiles.
Keep one thread per target and the existing interaction arithmetic and self-exclusion; ensure target-tail threads reach every CTA barrier.
Set block and items_per_block to 256; keep dynamic shared-memory launch allocation at zero because the 4,096 bytes are statically allocated.
